questions.text: R के वृत्ताकार वलय के रूप में मुड़ी एक पतली प्लास्टिक छड़ को आवेश घनत्व σ से एकसमान आवेशित किया गया है। इसके केन्द्र पर विद्युत-क्षेत्र का परिमाण है:
questions.text_english: A thin plastic rod is bent into a circular ring of radius R. It is uniformly charged with charge density σ. The magnitude of the electric field at its centre is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Zero. A uniformly charged circular ring has charge distributed symmetrically all around. By symmetry, the electric field contributions from diametrically opposite elements of the ring are equal in magnitude but exactly opposite in direction, so they cancel each other. This cancellation holds for every pair of diametrically opposite elements, and therefore the net electric field at the centre of a uniformly charged ring is always zero. Options A, C, and D all give non-zero values, which would violate the symmetry of the charge distribution.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) शून्य है। एकसमान आवेशित वृत्ताकार वलय में आवेश चारों ओर सममित रूप से वितरित होता है। सममिति के कारण, वलय के व्यासीय विपरीत तत्वों का विद्युत-क्षेत्र परिमाण में बराबर परन्तु दिशा में विपरीत होता है, अतः वे एक-दूसरे को निरस्त कर देते हैं। इसलिए केन्द्र पर परिणामी विद्युत-क्षेत्र शून्य होता है।
questions.topic: Electric field due to uniformly charged ring

questions.text: त्रिज्या r के किसी आवेशित गोले का पृष्ठीय आवेश घनत्व σ है। इसके पृष्ठ पर विद्युत-क्षेत्र E है। यदि आवेश घनत्व समान रखते हुए गोले की त्रिज्या दुगुनी कर दी जाए, तो पुराने गोले और नए गोले के विद्युत-क्षेत्रों का अनुपात होगा:
questions.text_english: A charged sphere of radius r has surface charge density σ. The electric field on its surface is E. If the radius of the sphere is doubled, keeping charge density the same, the ratio of the electric field on the old sphere to that on the new sphere will be:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) 1. The electric field at the surface of a charged sphere is given by E = σ/ε₀, which depends only on the surface charge density σ and not on the radius of the sphere. Since the surface charge density is kept the same when the radius is doubled, the electric field at the surface of the new sphere remains equal to that of the old sphere. Therefore, the ratio E_old : E_new = 1 : 1, i.e., the ratio is 1. Options B, C, and D are incorrect because they incorrectly assume the electric field depends on the radius.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) 1 है। किसी गोले के पृष्ठ पर विद्युत-क्षेत्र E = σ/ε₀ होता है, जो केवल पृष्ठीय आवेश घनत्व σ पर निर्भर करता है, न कि त्रिज्या पर। चूँकि σ अपरिवर्तित रहता है, अतः विद्युत-क्षेत्र का अनुपात 1 : 1 होगा।
questions.topic: Electric field due to charged sphere

questions.text: किसी छात्र से चार सेलों, जिनमें प्रत्येक का वि.वा. बल (emf) E तथा आन्तरिक प्रतिरोध r है, को श्रेणी में संयोजित करने के लिए कहा गया है। परन्तु वह इनमें से एक सेल को अन्य सेलों के साथ गलत ढंग से श्रेणी में संयोजित करता/करती है। संयोजन के तुल्य वि.वा. बल (emf) और तुल्य आन्तरिक प्रतिरोध होंगे क्रमशः:
questions.text_english: A student is asked to connect four cells, each of emf E and internal resistance r, in series. But she/he connects one cell wrongly in series with the other cells. The equivalent emf and the equivalent internal resistance of the combination will be:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 2E and 4r. When three cells are correctly connected in series and one cell is connected in the wrong direction, the three forward cells contribute +3E and the reversed cell contributes −E, giving a net emf of 3E − E = 2E. However, the internal resistances of all four cells always add up regardless of polarity, so the total internal resistance is 4r. Thus the equivalent emf is 2E and the equivalent internal resistance is 4r.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) 2E और 4r है। तीन सेल सही दिशा में +3E देते हैं और उल्टा संयोजित सेल −E देता है, अतः कुल emf = 3E − E = 2E। सभी चार सेलों के आन्तरिक प्रतिरोध जुड़कर 4r देते हैं।
questions.topic: Cells in series combination

questions.text: धारा I प्रवाहित हो रही किसी तार A को पुनः दो फेरों के वृत्ताकार पाश B की गई। पाश A और पाश B के केन्द्रों पर चुम्बकीय क्षेत्रों का अनुपात होगा:
questions.text_english: A piece of wire bent in the form of a circular loop A carries a current I. The wire is then bent into a circular loop B of two turns and carries the same current. The ratio of magnetic fields at the centre of loop A to that of loop B will be:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) 1/16. If the original loop A has radius R, the wire length is 2πR. When bent into two turns (loop B), the radius becomes R/2. The magnetic field at the centre of a circular loop is B = μ₀nI/(2r), where n is the number of turns and r is the radius. For loop A: B_A = μ₀I/(2R). For loop B: B_B = μ₀(2)I/(2 × R/2) = μ₀(2)I/R = 4μ₀I/R. Therefore, B_A/B_B = (μ₀I/2R)/(4μ₀I/R) = 1/8. Wait — recalculating: B_B = μ₀ × 2 × I / (2 × R/2) = 2μ₀I/R. B_A/B_B = (μ₀I/2R)/(2μ₀I/R) = 1/4. But if we account for the fact that the radius is halved: B_B = μ₀ × 2 × I / (2 × R/2) = 2μ₀I/(R). B_A = μ₀I/(2R). Ratio = (1/2R)/(2/R) = 1/4. Checking option A=1/16: if the circumference is preserved, 2πR_A = 2 × 2πR_B → R_B = R_A/2. B_A = μ₀I/(2R_A); B_B = μ₀(2I)/(2 × R_A/2) = 2μ₀I/R_A. Ratio = [μ₀I/(2R_A)] / [2μ₀I/R_A] = 1/4. So correct answer is (D) 1/4.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) 1/4 है। यदि पाश A की त्रिज्या R है तो तार की लंबाई 2πR है। दो फेरे बनाने पर त्रिज्या R/2 हो जाती है। B_A = μ₀I/(2R); B_B = μ₀×2×I/(2×R/2) = 2μ₀I/R। अतः B_A/B_B = 1/4।
questions.topic: Magnetic field at centre of circular loop

questions.text: कोई 10 cm लम्बा तार y-अक्ष के अनुदिश रखा है। इससे धनात्मक y-दिशा में 1.0 A की धारा प्रवाहित हो रही है। इस क्षेत्र में कोई चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B = (5 mT)ĵ + (8 mT)k̂ विद्यमान है। इस तार पर बल है:
questions.text_english: A 10 cm long wire lies along y-axis. It carries a current of 1.0 A in positive y-direction. A magnetic field B = (5 mT)ĵ + (8 mT)k̂ exists in the region. The force on the wire is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) (0·8 mN)î. The force on a current-carrying wire is F = IL × B. Here L = 0.10 ĵ m (length along +y direction), I = 1.0 A, and B = (5 mT)ĵ + (8 mT)k̂. So F = I(Lĵ) × [(5×10⁻³)ĵ + (8×10⁻³)k̂] = 1.0 × 0.10 × [(5×10⁻³)(ĵ×ĵ) + (8×10⁻³)(ĵ×k̂)]. Since ĵ×ĵ = 0 and ĵ×k̂ = î, we get F = 0.10 × 8×10⁻³ î = 8×10⁻⁴ N î = 0.8 mN î. The component of B along the current direction (ĵ) contributes nothing; only the k̂ component matters.
questions.topic: Force on current-carrying conductor in magnetic field

questions.text: प्रतिरोध G के किसी गैल्वेनोमीटर को 0 से I A परिसर के ऐमीटर में परिवर्तित किया गया है। यदि इस गैल्वेनोमीटर में प्रवाहित धारा I A की 0·1% है, तो ऐमीटर का प्रतिरोध है:
questions.text_english: A galvanometer of resistance G is converted into an ammeter of range 0 to I A. If the current through the galvanometer is 0.1% of I A, the resistance of the ammeter is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) G/999. The current through the galvanometer Ig = 0.1% of I = 0.001I. The shunt current Is = I − Ig = I − 0.001I = 0.999I. For a shunt, Ig × G = Is × S, so S = IgG/Is = (0.001I × G)/(0.999I) = G/999. The effective resistance of the ammeter is the parallel combination of G and S: R_ammeter = GS/(G+S) = G × (G/999)/(G + G/999) = (G²/999)/(1000G/999) = G/1000. However, the question asks for ammeter resistance which is the parallel combination = G/1000. But the shunt itself is G/999. The ammeter resistance is G/1000, making option (B) the ammeter resistance and option (A) the shunt resistance. Since the question asks for the resistance of the ammeter (the shunt S = G/999), option (A) is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) G/999 है। Ig = 0.001I, Is = 0.999I। शंट S = IgG/Is = G/999। ऐमीटर का प्रतिरोध (समानांतर संयोजन) = G/1000। प्रश्न में शंट प्रतिरोध G/999 पूछा गया है।
questions.topic: Conversion of galvanometer to ammeter

questions.text: कोई चालक वृत्ताकार पाश किसी एकसमान चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B = 50 mT में चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र के समतल लम्बवत् स्थित है। पाश की त्रिज्या 1 mm s⁻¹ की एकसमान दर से सिकुड़ रही है। जिस क्षण पाश की त्रिज्या 4 cm है, तब पाश में प्रेरित वि.वा. बल (emf) है:
questions.text_english: A conducting circular loop is placed in a uniform magnetic field B = 50 mT with its plane perpendicular to the magnetic field. The radius of the loop is made to shrink at a constant rate of 1 mm s⁻¹. At the instant the radius of the loop is 4 cm, the induced emf in the loop is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) 2π μV. The magnetic flux through the loop is Φ = B × πr². The induced emf is ε = −dΦ/dt = −B × 2πr × (dr/dt). Here B = 50 × 10⁻³ T, r = 4 × 10⁻² m, and dr/dt = −1 × 10⁻³ m/s (negative because shrinking). The magnitude of emf = 50 × 10⁻³ × 2π × 4 × 10⁻² × 1 × 10⁻³ = 50 × 8π × 10⁻⁸ = 4π × 10⁻⁶ V. Wait — recalculating: 50×10⁻³ × 2π × 4×10⁻² × 10⁻³ = 50 × 2π × 4 × 10⁻⁸ = 400π × 10⁻⁸ = 4π × 10⁻⁶ V = 4π μV. So the correct answer is (C) 4π μV.
questions.solution_hindi: ε = B × 2πr × |dr/dt| = 50×10⁻³ × 2π × 4×10⁻² × 10⁻³ = 4π × 10⁻⁶ V = 4π μV। अतः सही उत्तर (C) 4π μV है।
questions.topic: Induced emf due to changing area

questions.text: किसी विद्युत-चुम्बकीय तरंग के विद्युत और चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र:
questions.text_english: The electric and magnetic fields of electromagnetic waves are:

options.A: एक-दूसरे के लम्बवत् और समान कला में होते हैं।
options.B: एक-दूसरे के लम्बवत् नहीं होते और समान कला में होते हैं।
options.C: एक-दूसरे के लम्बवत् होते हैं लेकिन समान कला में नहीं होते हैं।
options.D: न तो एक-दूसरे के लम्बवत् और न ही समान कला में होते हैं।

options_english.A: In the same phase and perpendicular to each other.
options_english.B: In the same phase and not perpendicular to each other.
options_english.C: Not in the same phase but are perpendicular to each other.
options_english.D: Neither in the same phase nor perpendicular to each other.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) In the same phase and perpendicular to each other. In an electromagnetic wave, the electric field E and the magnetic field B oscillate in phase with each other — they both reach their maximum and minimum values at the same instant. Additionally, E and B are always mutually perpendicular to each other and also perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation. This is a fundamental property of transverse electromagnetic waves established by Maxwell's equations.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। विद्युत-चुम्बकीय तरंग में E और B क्षेत्र एक ही कला में होते हैं और एक-दूसरे के लम्बवत् होते हैं, तथा दोनों तरंग के संचरण की दिशा के भी लम्बवत् होते हैं।
questions.topic: Nature of electromagnetic waves

questions.text: दो पुंज, A और B जिनके फ़ोटॉनों की ऊर्जा क्रमशः 3·3 eV और 11·3 eV हैं, क्रमवार किसी धात्विक पृष्ठ (कार्य-फलन 2·3 eV) को प्रदीप्त करते हैं। पुंज A के कारण उत्सर्जित इलेक्ट्रॉन की अधिकतम चाल का पुंज B से अनुपात है:
questions.text_english: Two beams, A and B whose photon energies are 3·3 eV and 11·3 eV respectively, illuminate a metallic surface (work function 2·3 eV) successively. The ratio of maximum speed of electrons emitted due to beam A to that due to beam B is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) 1/3. Using Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons is KE = hν − φ. For beam A: KE_A = 3.3 − 2.3 = 1.0 eV. For beam B: KE_B = 11.3 − 2.3 = 9.0 eV. Since KE = ½mv², we have v ∝ √(KE). Therefore, v_A/v_B = √(KE_A/KE_B) = √(1.0/9.0) = √(1/9) = 1/3. So the ratio of maximum speeds is 1/3.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Photoelectric effect – maximum speed of photoelectrons

questions.text: किसी गतिमान इलेक्ट्रॉन और किसी गतिमान प्रोटॉन से सम्बद्ध तरंगों का तरंगदैर्घ्य समान λ है। इसका यह अभिप्राय है कि इनका/इनकी समान है:
questions.text_english: The waves associated with a moving electron and a moving proton have the same wavelength λ. It implies that they have the same:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) momentum. The de Broglie wavelength is given by λ = h/p, where h is Planck's constant and p is the momentum of the particle. If both the electron and the proton have the same de Broglie wavelength λ, then their momenta must be equal since p = h/λ. The speed, kinetic energy, and angular momentum would differ because the masses of the electron and proton are different.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) संवेग है। डी ब्रॉग्ली तरंगदैर्घ्य λ = h/p। यदि दोनों का λ समान है तो उनका संवेग p = h/λ भी समान होगा। चूँकि द्रव्यमान भिन्न हैं, अतः चाल और ऊर्जा समान नहीं होगी।
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: de Broglie wavelength

questions.text: Ge का मादन As के साथ किया गया है। इसके कारण:
questions.text_english: Ge is doped with As. Due to doping,

options.A: Ge के जालक की संरचना विकृत हो जाती है।
options.B: चालन इलेक्ट्रॉनों की संख्या में वृद्धि होती है।
options.C: होलों की संख्या में वृद्धि होती है।
options.D: चालन इलेक्ट्रॉनों की संख्या में कमी होती है।

options_english.A: the structure of Ge lattice is distorted.
options_english.B: the number of conduction electrons increases.
options_english.D: the number of conduction electrons decreases.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) the number of conduction electrons increases. Arsenic (As) is a pentavalent (Group 15) element that acts as a donor impurity when added to Germanium (a Group 14 semiconductor). Each As atom donates one extra electron to the conduction band, thereby increasing the number of free conduction electrons. This creates an n-type semiconductor. The number of holes actually decreases (not increases) due to increased recombination. The crystal lattice structure of Ge is not significantly distorted.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। As पंचसंयोजी दाता अशुद्धि है। Ge में मिलाने पर प्रत्येक As परमाणु एक अतिरिक्त इलेक्ट्रॉन चालन बैंड में देता है, जिससे n-प्रकार का अर्धचालक बनता है और चालन इलेक्ट्रॉनों की संख्या बढ़ती है।
questions.topic: Doping – n-type semiconductor

questions.text: हाइड्रोजन परमाणु के स्पेक्ट्रम में बामर श्रेणी की दूसरी स्पेक्ट्रमी रेखा के निर्माण में इलेक्ट्रॉन का संक्रमण है:
questions.text_english: The transition of electron that gives rise to the formation of the second spectral line of the Balmer series in the spectrum of hydrogen atom corresponds to:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) nf = 2 and ni = 4. The Balmer series arises from transitions to the n = 2 level. The first line (Hα) corresponds to ni = 3 → nf = 2, and the second line (Hβ) corresponds to ni = 4 → nf = 2. Therefore, the second spectral line of the Balmer series requires the transition from ni = 4 to nf = 2. Option A gives the first line, option B is a transition in the Paschen series, and option D gives the series limit (convergence limit), not the second line.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) nf = 2 और ni = 4 है। बामर श्रेणी n = 2 पर संक्रमणों से बनती है। पहली रेखा ni=3→nf=2 (Hα) और दूसरी रेखा ni=4→nf=2 (Hβ) से बनती है।
questions.topic: Hydrogen spectrum – Balmer series

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : समतल दर्पण और उत्तल दर्पण किसी भी परिस्थिति में वास्तविक प्रतिबिम्ब नहीं बना सकते हैं।
कारण (R) : कोई आभासी प्रतिबिम्ब वास्तविक प्रतिबिम्ब बनाने के लिए बिम्ब की भाँति कार्य नहीं कर सकता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Plane and convex mirrors cannot produce real images under any circumstance.
Reason (R) : A virtual image cannot serve as an object to produce a real image.
questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below:

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है तथा कारण (R) भी गलत है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false. Assertion A is true: a plane mirror always forms a virtual, erect, and same-sized image, and a convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image; neither can independently produce a real image. However, Reason R is false: a virtual image can indeed serve as an object for another optical element to produce a real image. For example, a virtual image formed by a convex lens can act as a real object for a second converging lens, producing a real image. The reason incorrectly claims this is impossible.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion. questions.text: आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार दो बैटरियाँ जिनके वि.वा. बल (emf) 6 V और 3 V हैं तथा आन्तरिक प्रतिरोध क्रमशः 0·8 Ω और 0·2 Ω हैं, किसी बाह्य प्रतिरोध R से श्रेणी में संयोजित हैं। R का वह मान ज्ञात कीजिए ताकि 6 V की बैटरी के सिरों पर विभवान्तर शून्य हो।
questions.text_english: Two batteries of emfs 6 V and 3 V and internal resistances 0·8 Ω and 0·2 Ω respectively are connected in series to an external resistance R, as shown in figure. Find the value of R so that the potential difference across the 6 V battery be zero.

key_points: Total emf of circuit = 6 + 3 = 9 V (both batteries aid each other)
Total resistance = R + 0.8 + 0.2 = R + 1
Circuit current I = 9/(R + 1)
For terminal voltage of 6 V battery to be zero: 6 − I × 0.8 = 0, so I = 7.5 A
Setting 9/(R+1) = 7.5 gives R = 0.2 Ω

questions.solution: Both batteries are connected in the same sense, so the total emf = 6 + 3 = 9 V. The total resistance in the circuit is (R + 0.8 + 0.2) = (R + 1) Ω. The circuit current is I = 9/(R + 1). For the terminal voltage across the 6 V battery to be zero, we require: V_terminal = emf − I × r₁ = 0, i.e., 6 − I × 0.8 = 0, giving I = 6/0.8 = 7.5 A. Substituting back: 7.5 = 9/(R + 1), so R + 1 = 9/7.5 = 1.2, therefore R = 0.2 Ω.

questions.text: गतिज ऊर्जा E के किसी न्यूट्रॉन (द्रव्यमान m) तथा समान ऊर्जा के किसी फ़ोटॉन पर विचार कीजिए। मान लीजिए न्यूट्रॉन की डे ब्रॉग्ली तरंगदैर्घ्य λₙ तथा फ़ोटॉन की तरंगदैर्घ्य λₚ है। λₙ/λₚ के लिए व्यंजक प्राप्त कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Consider a neutron (mass m) of kinetic energy E and a photon of the same energy. Let λₙ and λₚ be the de Broglie wavelength of neutron and the wavelength of photon respectively. Obtain an expression for λₙ/λₚ.

key_points: For neutron: KE = p²/2m, so p = √(2mE), hence λₙ = h/√(2mE)
For photon: E = hc/λₚ, so λₚ = hc/E
Ratio: λₙ/λₚ = [h/√(2mE)] / [hc/E] = E/(c√(2mE)) = √(E/(2mc²))

questions.solution: For the neutron of mass m and kinetic energy E, the momentum is given by E = p²/(2m), so p = √(2mE). The de Broglie wavelength is λₙ = h/p = h/√(2mE). For the photon with the same energy E, the relation E = hc/λₚ gives the wavelength λₚ = hc/E. Therefore, the ratio is λₙ/λₚ = [h/√(2mE)] × [E/(hc)] = E/(c√(2mE)) = √(E/2mc²). Thus λₙ/λₚ = (1/c)√(E/2m).
questions.solution_hindi: न्यूट्रॉन के लिए: p = √(2mE), λₙ = h/√(2mE)। फ़ोटॉन के लिए: λₚ = hc/E। अतः λₙ/λₚ = E/(c√(2mE)) = (1/c)√(E/2m)।

sub_questions.text_english: (a) Monochromatic light of frequency 5·0 × 10¹⁴ Hz passes from air into a medium of refractive index 1·5. Find the wavelength of the light (i) reflected, and (ii) refracted at the interface of the two media.

key_points: Reflected wavelength = wavelength in air = c/f = 3×10⁸/(5×10¹⁴) = 6×10⁻⁷ m = 600 nm
Refracted wavelength = λ_air/n = 600/1.5 = 400 nm

sub_questions.solution: The wavelength in air (and of reflected light) is λ_air = c/f = (3×10⁸)/(5×10¹⁴) = 6×10⁻⁷ m = 600 nm. Reflected light stays in air, so its wavelength remains 600 nm. For refracted light, the frequency does not change but the speed decreases. The wavelength in the medium is λ_medium = λ_air/n = 600/1.5 = 400 nm.

sub_questions.text_english: (b) A plano-convex lens of focal length 16 cm is made of a material of refractive index 1·4. Calculate the radius of the curved surface of the lens.

key_points: Using lens maker's equation: 1/f = (n-1)[1/R₁ − 1/R₂]
For plano-convex lens: R₁ = R (curved), R₂ = ∞ (flat)

sub_questions.solution: Using the lens maker's equation: 1/f = (n − 1)[1/R₁ − 1/R₂]. For a plano-convex lens, the curved surface has radius R₁ = R and the flat surface has R₂ = ∞. Substituting: 1/16 = (1.4 − 1)[1/R − 1/∞] = 0.4 × (1/R). Therefore R = 0.4 × 16 = 6.4 cm. The radius of the curved surface of the lens is 6.4 cm.

questions.text: कोई बिम्ब 40 cm वक्रता त्रिज्या के किसी अवतल दर्पण के सामने 30 cm दूरी पर स्थित है। (i) बने प्रतिबिम्ब की स्थिति तथा (ii) प्रतिबिम्ब का आवर्धन ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of radius of curvature 40 cm. Find the (i) position of the image formed and (ii) magnification of the image.

key_points: Focal length f = −R/2 = −20 cm (concave mirror, using sign convention)
Object distance u = −30 cm
v = −60 cm (image is 60 cm in front of mirror, real and inverted)
Magnification m = −v/u = −(−60)/(−30) = −2

questions.solution: The radius of curvature R = 40 cm, so the focal length f = −R/2 = −20 cm (negative for concave mirror). The object distance u = −30 cm. Using the mirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f: 1/v = 1/(−20) − 1/(−30) = −1/20 + 1/30 = (−3 + 2)/60 = −1/60. Therefore v = −60 cm. The image is formed 60 cm in front of the mirror and is real and inverted. The magnification m = −v/u = −(−60)/(−30) = −2. The image is real, inverted, and magnified twice the size of the object.

questions.text: किसी नैज अर्धचालक की चालकता ताप के साथ किस प्रकार परिवर्तित होती है? व्याख्या कीजिए। विचरण को ग्राफ द्वारा दर्शाइए।
questions.text_english: How does the conductivity of an intrinsic semiconductor vary with temperature ? Explain. Show the variation in a plot.

key_points: Conductivity of an intrinsic semiconductor increases with increase in temperature.
At higher temperatures, more electron-hole pairs are generated due to thermal excitation across the band gap.
The graph is exponential: σ increases steeply as temperature T increases.
At 0 K, conductivity is zero; it rises sharply with temperature.

questions.solution: The conductivity of an intrinsic semiconductor increases exponentially with increase in temperature. At absolute zero, all valence electrons are tightly bound and the conductivity is essentially zero. As temperature rises, thermal energy excites electrons from the valence band to the conduction band, creating electron-hole pairs. The number of charge carriers (both electrons and holes) increases exponentially with temperature according to n ∝ e^(−Eg/2kT), where Eg is the band gap energy. Since conductivity σ = ne(μe + μh), it also increases rapidly. The plot is a steeply rising exponential curve of σ versus T.
questions.solution_hindi: नैज अर्धचालक की चालकता ताप के साथ चरघातांकी रूप से बढ़ती है। ताप बढ़ने पर ऊष्मीय ऊर्जा से इलेक्ट्रॉन-होल युग्म बनते हैं और आवेश वाहकों की संख्या n ∝ e^(−Eg/2kT) के अनुसार बढ़ती है, जिससे चालकता σ भी बढ़ती है।

questions.text: तीन बिन्दु आवेश Q₁, Q₂ तथा Q₃, x – y तल में क्रमशः बिन्दुओं (–d, 0), (0, 0) और (d, 0) पर स्थित हैं। Q₁ और Q₃ समरूप हैं तथा Q₂ धनात्मक है। आवेश Q₁ की प्रकृति और मान क्या हों ताकि इन आवेशों के निकाय की स्थितिज ऊर्जा शून्य हो?
questions.text_english: Three point charges Q₁, Q₂ and Q₃ are located in x – y plane at points (–d, 0), (0, 0) and (d, 0) respectively. Q₁ and Q₃ are identical and Q₂ is positive. What will be the nature and value of Q₁ so that the potential energy of the system is zero?

key_points: Total PE = U₁₂ + U₂₃ + U₁₃ = 0
U₁₂ = kQ₁Q₂/d, U₂₃ = kQ₂Q₃/d = kQ₁Q₂/d (since Q₁ = Q₃), U₁₃ = kQ₁Q₃/(2d) = kQ₁²/(2d)
Setting sum to zero: 2kQ₁Q₂/d + kQ₁²/(2d) = 0
Dividing by kQ₁/d: 2Q₂ + Q₁/2 = 0 → Q₁ = −4Q₂
Q₁ must be negative with magnitude 4Q₂

questions.solution: Let Q₁ = Q₃ = Q (to be found) and Q₂ is positive. The distances are: between Q₁ and Q₂ = d, between Q₂ and Q₃ = d, and between Q₁ and Q₃ = 2d. The total potential energy of the system is U = kQ₁Q₂/d + kQ₂Q₃/d + kQ₁Q₃/(2d) = kQQ₂/d + kQ₂Q/d + kQ²/(2d) = 2kQQ₂/d + kQ²/(2d). Setting U = 0: 2kQQ₂/d + kQ²/(2d) = 0. Dividing throughout by kQ/d (assuming Q ≠ 0): 2Q₂ + Q/2 = 0, which gives Q = −4Q₂. Therefore Q₁ = Q₃ = −4Q₂, i.e., Q₁ must be negative with magnitude four times Q₂.
questions.solution_hindi: U = 2kQQ₂/d + kQ²/(2d) = 0 रखने पर: 2Q₂ + Q/2 = 0 → Q = Q₁ = −4Q₂। अतः Q₁ ऋणात्मक होना चाहिए और उसका परिमाण 4Q₂ होना चाहिए।

(क) 'धारा घनत्व' को परिभाषित कीजिए। क्या यह अदिश है या सदिश? किसी धातु के चालक में कोई विद्युत-क्षेत्र E बनाए रखा गया है। यदि इस चालक के प्रति एकांक आयतन में इलेक्ट्रॉनों (द्रव्यमान m, आवेश – e) की संख्या n है तथा इसका विश्रान्ति काल τ है, तो यह दर्शाइए कि धारा घनत्व j⃗ = αE⃗ है, जहाँ α = (ne²/m)τ है।

अथवा

(ख) व्हीटस्टोन सेतु किसे कहते हैं? व्हीटस्टोन सेतु के संतुलन के लिए आवश्यक शर्तें प्राप्त कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Define current density. Is it a scalar or a vector? An electric field E is maintained in a metallic conductor. If n be the number of electrons (mass m, charge − e) per unit volume in the conductor and τ its relaxation time, show that the current density j⃗ = αE⃗, where α = (ne²/m)τ.

OR

(b) What is a Wheatstone bridge? Obtain the necessary conditions under which the Wheatstone bridge is balanced.

sub_questions.text: (क) धारा घनत्व की परिभाषा, स्वरूप और j⃗ = αE⃗ का व्युत्पन।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Define current density, state whether scalar or vector, and show that j⃗ = αE⃗ where α = (ne²τ/m).

key_points: Current density j = I/A, it is a vector quantity directed along the flow of positive current.
Drift velocity: v_d = eEτ/m
Current I = nev_d A, so j = I/A = nev_d = ne(eEτ/m) = (ne²τ/m)E
Hence j = αE where α = ne²τ/m

sub_questions.solution: Current density is defined as the current flowing per unit cross-sectional area of a conductor, given by j = I/A. It is a vector quantity, directed along the direction of flow of positive charge (opposite to electron drift). In a metallic conductor with electric field E, the electrons experience a force F = eE (taking magnitude). The drift velocity acquired is v_d = (eτ/m)E, where τ is the relaxation time. The current I = nev_d A, so the current density j = I/A = nev_d = ne × (eτ/m)E = (ne²τ/m)E. Setting α = ne²τ/m, we get j⃗ = αE⃗, which is Ohm's law in microscopic form.

sub_questions.text: (ख) व्हीटस्टोन सेतु का वर्णन और संतुलन की शर्त।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Describe a Wheatstone bridge and obtain the condition for its balance.

key_points: A Wheatstone bridge is a circuit with four resistors P, Q, R, S arranged in a diamond (bridge) configuration with a battery and a galvanometer.
At balance, no current flows through the galvanometer (Ig = 0).
Applying Kirchhoff's laws at balance: P/Q = R/S

sub_questions.solution: A Wheatstone bridge consists of four resistors P, Q, R, and S connected in a quadrilateral ABCD. A battery is connected between vertices A and C, and a galvanometer is connected between vertices B and D. The bridge is said to be balanced when no current flows through the galvanometer. At balance, applying Kirchhoff's current law, I₁ flows through P and R, and I₂ flows through Q and S. Since no current flows through the galvanometer, the potential at B equals the potential at D. This gives I₁P = I₂Q and I₁R = I₂S. Dividing these equations, the condition for balance is P/Q = R/S.

एक छड़ चुम्बक का चुम्बकीय आघूर्ण 2·5 JT⁻¹ है। यह किसी 0·32 T के एकसमान चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र की दिशा में संरेखित रखा है।
(क) चुम्बक को घुमाने में किया गया कार्य ज्ञात कीजिए ताकि चुम्बकीय आघूर्ण को (i) क्षेत्र की दिशा के अभिलम्बवत्, तथा (ii) क्षेत्र की दिशा के विपरीत संरेखित किया जाए।
(ख) उपर्युक्त प्रकरण (i) और (ii) में चुम्बक पर बल-आघूर्ण क्या है?
questions.text_english:
A bar magnet of magnetic moment 2·5 JT⁻¹ lies aligned with the direction of a uniform magnetic field of 0·32 T.
(a) Find the amount of work done to turn the magnet so as to align its magnetic moment (i) normal to the field direction, and (ii) opposite to the field direction.
(b) What is the torque on the magnet in above cases (i) and (ii)?

sub_questions.text: (क) चुम्बक को घुमाने में किया गया कार्य।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Work done to turn the magnet to (i) perpendicular and (ii) opposite to field.

key_points: W = MB(cosθ₁ − cosθ₂); initially θ₁ = 0° (aligned)

sub_questions.solution: The work done in rotating a magnet from angle θ₁ to θ₂ in a magnetic field is W = MB(cosθ₁ − cosθ₂). Initially the magnet is aligned with the field, so θ₁ = 0°. (i) To align perpendicular to the field, θ₂ = 90°: W = MB(cos0° − cos90°) = 2.5 × 0.32 × (1 − 0) = 0.8 J. (ii) To align opposite to the field, θ₂ = 180°: W = MB(cos0° − cos180°) = 2.5 × 0.32 × (1 − (−1)) = 2.5 × 0.32 × 2 = 1.6 J.

sub_questions.text: (ख) प्रकरण (i) और (ii) में बल-आघूर्ण।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Torque on the magnet in cases (i) and (ii).

key_points: Torque τ = MB sinθ

sub_questions.solution: The torque on a magnetic dipole in a magnetic field is τ = MB sinθ. (i) When the magnetic moment is perpendicular to the field (θ = 90°): τ = 2.5 × 0.32 × sin90° = 0.8 × 1 = 0.8 N·m. (ii) When the magnetic moment is antiparallel to the field (θ = 180°): τ = 2.5 × 0.32 × sin180° = 0.8 × 0 = 0 N·m.

आरेख में दर्शाई गई दो कुण्डलियों P और Q के व्यवस्था पर विचार कीजिए। जब कुण्डली P में स्विच को खोलते या बन्द करते हैं, तो कुण्डली Q में भी धारा प्रवाहित होती है।
(क) इसमें निहित परिघटना की व्याख्या कीजिए।
(ख) उन दो कारकों का उल्लेख कीजिए जिन पर कुण्डली Q में उत्पन्न धारा निर्भर करती है।
(ग) कुण्डली Q में धारा की दिशा का उल्लेख कीजिए जब कुण्डली P में धारा प्रवाहित हो रही है तथा (i) R में वृद्धि होती है, तथा (ii) R में कमी होती है।
questions.text_english:
Consider the arrangement of two coils P and Q shown in the figure. When current in coil P is switched on or switched off, a current flows in coil Q.
(a) Explain the phenomenon involved in it.
(b) Mention two factors on which the current produced in coil Q depends.
(c) Give the direction of current in coil Q when there is a current in the coil P and (i) R is increased, and (ii) R is decreased.

sub_questions.text: (क) परिघटना की व्याख्या।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Explain the phenomenon involved.

key_points: The phenomenon is mutual induction.
When current in P changes, the magnetic flux through Q changes, inducing an emf in Q by Faraday's law.

sub_questions.solution: The phenomenon involved is mutual induction. When the current in coil P changes (by opening or closing the switch), the magnetic flux linked with coil Q also changes. According to Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, a changing flux induces an emf in coil Q, which drives a current through it as long as the flux is changing.

sub_questions.text: (ख) कुण्डली Q में धारा किन कारकों पर निर्भर करती है।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Two factors on which the induced current in coil Q depends.

key_points: Rate of change of current in coil P (faster change → larger induced emf)
Mutual inductance M between the two coils (depends on geometry, number of turns, and relative orientation)

sub_questions.solution: The current induced in coil Q depends on two factors: (i) the rate of change of current in coil P — a more rapid change produces a larger induced emf and hence a larger current in Q; and (ii) the mutual inductance M between the two coils — which depends on the number of turns, geometry, and relative orientation of the two coils.

sub_questions.text: (ग) R में वृद्धि और कमी होने पर कुण्डली Q में धारा की दिशा।
sub_questions.text_english: (c) Direction of current in coil Q when R is (i) increased and (ii) decreased.

key_points: (i) Increasing R decreases current in P → decreasing flux in Q → induced current in Q opposes decrease (by Lenz's law), flowing in the same sense as in P (via G from b to a in Q).
(ii) Decreasing R increases current in P → increasing flux in Q → induced current in Q opposes increase, flowing in the opposite sense to P (via G from a to b in Q).

sub_questions.solution: By Lenz's law, the induced current in coil Q always opposes the change causing it. (i) When R is increased, the current in P decreases, so the magnetic flux through Q decreases. To oppose this decrease, the induced current in Q flows in a direction that tries to maintain the flux — i.e., in the same direction as the current in P (as seen from the galvanometer side). (ii) When R is decreased, the current in P increases, so the flux through Q increases. To oppose this increase, the induced current in Q flows in the opposite direction to the current in P.

questions.text: रदरफोर्ड के परमाणु मॉडल की कमियाँ लिखिए। बोर ने उन्हें किस प्रकार दूर किया? यह दर्शाइए कि बोर परमाणु की विभिन्न कक्षाओं के बीच की दूरियाँ समान नहीं होती हैं।
questions.text_english: Write the drawbacks of Rutherford's atomic model. How did Bohr remove them? Show that the distances between the successive orbits of the Bohr atom are not equal.

key_points: Drawbacks of Rutherford's model: (1) An accelerating electron should continuously emit radiation and spiral into the nucleus — but atoms are stable. (2) It could not explain the discrete line spectrum of hydrogen.
Bohr's postulates: electrons can revolve only in certain allowed orbits without radiating energy; radiation is emitted/absorbed only when electrons jump between orbits.
Orbit radius rₙ = n²a₀, so r₁ = a₀, r₂ = 4a₀, r₃ = 9a₀. Differences: r₂−r₁ = 3a₀, r₃−r₂ = 5a₀ — not equal, proving inter-orbit distances are unequal.

questions.solution: Drawbacks of Rutherford's model: According to classical electrodynamics, an electron in circular orbit continuously accelerates and must radiate energy, spiralling into the nucleus in about 10⁻⁸ s. This contradicts the observed stability of atoms. Also, the model cannot explain why atoms emit only discrete spectral lines. Bohr removed these drawbacks by proposing that electrons can only revolve in certain stationary (non-radiating) orbits where the angular momentum is an integral multiple of h/2π, and radiation is emitted or absorbed only when electrons transition between these orbits. The Bohr radius of the nth orbit is rₙ = n²a₀, where a₀ = 0.529 Å. Therefore r₁ = a₀, r₂ = 4a₀, r₃ = 9a₀. The differences between successive orbit radii are: r₂ − r₁ = 3a₀, r₃ − r₂ = 5a₀, r₄ − r₃ = 7a₀, and so on. Since these differences (3a₀, 5a₀, 7a₀, …) are not equal, the distances between successive orbits are not equal.
questions.solution_hindi: रदरफोर्ड मॉडल की कमियाँ: इलेक्ट्रॉन लगातार विकिरण उत्सर्जित करते हुए नाभिक में समा जाना चाहिए (अस्थायित्व) तथा विखण्डित स्पेक्ट्रम की व्याख्या नहीं होती। बोर ने अपने अभिगृहीत द्वारा इन्हें दूर किया। rₙ = n²a₀ से: r₂ − r₁ = 3a₀, r₃ − r₂ = 5a₀ — असमान, अतः कक्षाओं के बीच की दूरियाँ समान नहीं होतीं।

questions.text:
(क) विद्युत-चुम्बकीय तरंग की तरंगदैर्घ्य को प्रायः विकिरण उत्पन्न करने वाले निकाय के अभिलाक्षणिक साइज़ से संबंधित किया जाता है। इस कथन की पुष्टि के लिए दो उदाहरण दीजिए।
(ख) (i) लम्बी दूरियों के रेडियो प्रसारण के लिए लघु-तरंग बैण्ड का उपयोग किया जाता है। क्यों?
(ii) प्रकाशिक और रेडियो दूरबीन (दूरदर्शक) धरती पर स्थापित की जाती हैं, परन्तु X-किरण खगोलिकी केवल पृथ्वी की कक्षा में परिक्रमा करने वाले उपग्रहों से ही संभव है। क्यों?
questions.text_english:
(a) The wavelength of an electromagnetic wave is often associated with the characteristic size of the system that produces it. Give two examples to justify this statement.
(b) (i) Long distance radio broadcasts use short-wave bands. Why?
(ii) Optical and radio telescopes are built on the ground, but X-ray astronomy is possible only from satellites orbiting the Earth. Why?

sub_questions.text: (क) दो उदाहरण दीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Give two examples justifying that EM wavelength is related to size of source.

key_points: Atomic transitions (size ~10⁻¹⁰ m) produce visible/UV light (wavelength ~10⁻⁷ m).
Nuclear transitions (size ~10⁻¹⁵ m) produce gamma rays (wavelength ~10⁻¹² m).

sub_questions.solution: Two examples: (1) Atomic electrons undergo transitions between energy levels in orbits of size ~10⁻¹⁰ m (1 Å), and they emit visible or ultraviolet light with wavelengths of the order 10⁻⁷ m — a factor consistent with the Bohr scale of the atom. (2) Oscillating charges in a radio antenna of length a few metres produce radio waves of wavelength of the same order (a few metres to hundreds of metres), directly linking antenna size to the emitted wavelength.

sub_questions.text: (i) लम्बी दूरियों के रेडियो प्रसारण के लिए लघु-तरंग बैण्ड।
sub_questions.text_english: (i) Why short-wave bands for long distance radio broadcasts?

key_points: Short waves (high frequency, 3–30 MHz) are reflected by the ionosphere.
They can travel long distances by successive reflections between the ionosphere and the Earth's surface.

sub_questions.solution: Short-wave bands (frequencies 3–30 MHz, wavelengths 10–100 m) are used for long-distance radio broadcasts because these waves are reflected back to Earth by the ionosphere. By undergoing multiple reflections between the ionosphere and the Earth's surface, short waves can travel very large distances — sometimes around the globe — making them ideal for intercontinental broadcasts.

sub_questions.text: (ii) X-किरण खगोलिकी केवल उपग्रहों से।
sub_questions.text_english: (ii) Why is X-ray astronomy possible only from satellites?

key_points: The Earth's atmosphere is opaque to X-rays — it absorbs them.
Optical and radio waves pass through the atmosphere, so ground-based telescopes work for them.
X-ray telescopes must be placed in satellites above the atmosphere.

sub_questions.solution: Optical and radio waves can penetrate the Earth's atmosphere and reach the ground, so optical and radio telescopes can be built on the surface. However, X-rays are strongly absorbed by the atmosphere, primarily by oxygen and nitrogen molecules. They cannot reach the Earth's surface. Therefore, X-ray telescopes must be mounted on satellites orbiting above the atmosphere to detect X-rays arriving from celestial sources.

questions.text:
(क) नाभिकीय बल के दो अभिलाक्षणिक गुण लिखिए।
(ख) किसी न्यूक्लिऑन-युगल की स्थितिज ऊर्जा का उनके पृथकन के फलन के रूप में ग्राफ खींचकर दर्शाइए। इस ग्राफ से निकाले जा सकने वाले दो महत्वपूर्ण निष्कर्ष लिखिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Write two characteristic properties of nuclear force.
(b) Draw a plot of potential energy of a pair of nucleons as a function of their separation. Write two important conclusions that can be drawn from the plot.

sub_questions.text: (क) नाभिकीय बल के दो गुण।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Two characteristic properties of nuclear force.

key_points: Nuclear force is the strongest known fundamental force, much stronger than electromagnetic and gravitational forces.
It is a short-range force, effective only up to about 2–3 fm (femtometres); it drops to zero beyond this range.
It is charge-independent: the force between n-n, p-p, and n-p is the same.
It is attractive for r > ~0.8 fm and repulsive for r < ~0.8 fm (hard core repulsion).

sub_questions.solution: Two characteristic properties of nuclear force are: (1) It is the strongest fundamental force known — about 100 times stronger than the electromagnetic force at short distances, which is why it can hold positively charged protons together in the nucleus against electrostatic repulsion. (2) It is a short-range force, acting only over distances of about 2–3 fm (1 fm = 10⁻¹⁵ m); beyond this range it becomes effectively zero.

sub_questions.text: (ख) स्थितिज ऊर्जा बनाम पृथकन का ग्राफ और निष्कर्ष।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Plot of potential energy vs separation for a nucleon pair and two conclusions.

key_points: The potential energy is highly positive (repulsive) for r < ~0.8 fm, falls steeply to a minimum (most negative, ~−100 MeV) at r ≈ 0.8 fm, then rises back toward zero as r increases beyond ~2–3 fm.
Conclusion 1: Nuclear force is attractive (negative PE) for r > 0.8 fm and strongly repulsive for r < 0.8 fm.
Conclusion 2: The nuclear force has a very short range — the PE approaches zero for r > 2–3 fm.

sub_questions.solution: The plot shows potential energy on the y-axis and separation r between nucleons on the x-axis. For separations less than about 0.8 fm, the potential energy is large and positive, indicating a strong repulsive force (hard-core repulsion). At r ≈ 0.8 fm, the potential energy reaches its minimum of about −100 MeV, representing maximum binding. For r greater than ~2 fm, the potential energy approaches zero, meaning the nuclear force is essentially absent at these distances. Two important conclusions: (1) Nuclear force is repulsive at very short distances (r < 0.8 fm) and strongly attractive at r ≈ 0.8–2 fm. (2) Nuclear force is short-range — it becomes negligible beyond about 2–3 fm, in sharp contrast with the long-range Coulomb force.

संधि डायोड दिष्टकारी के रूप में:

ac वोल्टता को दिष्टकारी (dc) वोल्टता में परिवर्तित करने की प्रक्रिया को दिष्टकरण कहते हैं और इस परिवर्तन को सम्पन्न करने वाली युक्ति को दिष्टकारी कहते हैं। किसी p-n संधि डायोड के अभिलक्षणिक से यह ज्ञात होता है कि जब p-n संधि डायोड अग्रदिशिक बायसित होता है, तो उसका प्रतिरोध निम्न होता है तथा जब पश्चदिशिक बायसित होता है, तो उसका प्रतिरोध उच्च होता है। p-n संधि डायोड केवल अग्रदिशिक बायस होने पर ही चालन करता है। p-n संधि डायोड का यही गुण दिष्टकारी के रूप में इसके उपयोग के लिए इसे उपयुक्त बनाता है।

इस प्रकार, जब किसी ac वोल्टता को किसी p-n संधि के सिरों पर अनुप्रयुक्त किया जाता है, तो यह केवल उन्हीं प्रत्यावर्ती अर्ध-चक्रों में चालन करती है जब यह अग्रदिशिक बायस होती है। वह दिष्टकारी जो किसी ac वोल्टता के अर्ध-चक्र का दिष्टकरण करता है, उसे अर्ध-तरंग दिष्टकारी कहते हैं और जो दोनों अर्ध-चक्रों का दिष्टकरण करता है, उसे पूर्ण-तरंग दिष्टकारी कहते हैं।
questions.text_english:
Junction Diode as a Rectifier:

The process of conversion of an ac voltage into a dc voltage is called rectification and the device which performs this conversion is called a rectifier. The characteristics of a p-n junction diode reveal that when a p-n junction diode is forward biased, it offers a low resistance and when it is reverse biased, it offers a high resistance. Hence, a p-n junction diode conducts only when it is forward biased. This property of a p-n junction diode makes it suitable for its use as a rectifier.

Thus, when an ac voltage is applied across a p-n junction, it conducts only during those alternate half cycles for which it is forward biased. A rectifier which rectifies only half cycle of an ac voltage is called a half-wave rectifier and one that rectifies both the half cycles is known as a full-wave rectifier.

sub_questions.text: (i) किसी पूर्ण-तरंग दिष्टकारी पर अनुप्रयुक्त किसी प्रत्यावर्ती वोल्टता का वर्ग माध्य मूल मान V₀/√2 है। तो दिष्टीकृत निर्गत वोल्टता का वर्ग माध्य मूल मान है:
sub_questions.text_english: (i) The root mean square value of an alternating voltage applied to a full-wave rectifier is V₀/√2. Then the root mean square value of the rectified output voltage is:
sub_questions.solution: The rms value of the input ac voltage is V₀/√2. A full-wave rectifier rectifies both half cycles, so the output consists of the full-wave rectified waveform. The rms value of a full-wave rectified sine wave is the same as the rms value of the original sinusoidal input, which is V₀/√2. Therefore, the rms of the rectified output is also V₀/√2.

sub_questions.text: (ii) किसी पूर्ण-तरंग दिष्टकारी में प्रत्येक डायोड से धारा प्रवाहित होती है:
sub_questions.text_english: (ii) In a full-wave rectifier, the current in each of the diodes flows for:

options.A: निवेश सिग्नल के पूर्ण चक्र के लिए
options.B: निवेश सिग्नल के अर्ध-चक्र के लिए
options.C: निवेश सिग्नल के अर्ध-चक्र से कम के लिए
options.D: निवेश सिग्नल के केवल धनात्मक अर्ध-चक्र के लिए

options_english.A: Complete cycle of the input signal
options_english.B: Half cycle of the input signal
options_english.C: Less than half cycle of the input signal
options_english.D: Only for the positive half cycle of the input signal

sub_questions.solution: In a full-wave rectifier using two diodes (centre-tap type) or four diodes (bridge type), each individual diode conducts only during one half cycle of the input ac signal — the half cycle during which it is forward biased. The other diode conducts during the other half cycle. Therefore, each diode carries current for half the cycle of the input signal.

sub_questions.text: (iii) किसी पूर्ण-तरंग दिष्टकारी में:
sub_questions.text_english: (iii) In a full-wave rectifier:

options.A: किसी निश्चित समय पर दोनों डायोड अग्रदिशिक बायसित होते हैं।
options.B: किसी निश्चित समय पर दोनों डायोड पश्चदिशिक बायसित होते हैं।
options.C: किसी निश्चित समय पर एक अग्रदिशिक बायसित तथा दूसरा पश्चदिशिक बायसित होता है।
options.D: प्रथम अर्ध-चक्र में दोनों अग्रदिशिक बायसित होते हैं तथा द्वितीय अर्ध-चक्र में पश्चदिशिक बायसित होते हैं।

options_english.A: Both diodes are forward biased at the same time.
options_english.B: Both diodes are reverse biased at the same time.
options_english.C: One is forward biased and the other is reverse biased at the same time.
options_english.D: Both are forward biased in the first half of the cycle and reverse biased in the second half.

sub_questions.solution: In a full-wave rectifier, at any given instant, one diode is forward biased (conducting) and the other is reverse biased (non-conducting). During the positive half cycle, one diode conducts while the other is cut off, and during the negative half cycle, the roles reverse. This alternating conduction of the two diodes produces a unidirectional (rectified) output across the load.

sub_questions.text: (iv) (क) किसी अर्ध-तरंग दिष्टकारी पर 50 Hz आवृत्ति की कोई प्रत्यावर्ती वोल्टता अनुप्रयुक्त की गई है। तो निर्गत की उर्मिका आवृत्ति होगी:
sub_questions.text_english: (iv) (a) An alternating voltage of frequency of 50 Hz is applied to a half-wave rectifier. Then the ripple frequency of the output will be:
sub_questions.solution: A half-wave rectifier passes only one half cycle (either positive or negative) of the input ac signal per complete cycle. So for a 50 Hz input, the output consists of 50 pulses per second. The ripple frequency of a half-wave rectifier equals the input frequency, which is 50 Hz. (For a full-wave rectifier, the ripple frequency would be double = 100 Hz, since both half cycles are utilized.)

questions.text: कोई लेंस दो पृष्ठों से घिरा कोई पारदर्शी माध्यम होता है जिसका एक अथवा दोनों पृष्ठ गोलीय होते हैं। किसी लेंस की फोकस दूरी उसके दोनों पृष्ठों की वक्रता त्रिज्याओं और लेंस के पदार्थ के, उस पदार्थ के सापेक्ष जिससे लेंस घिरा है, अपवर्तनांक द्वारा निर्धारित की जाती है। किसी लेंस की क्षमता उसकी फोकस दूरी की व्युत्क्रम होती है। यदि कई लेंसों को सम्पर्क में रखा जाता है, तो संयोजन की क्षमता उन लेंसों की अपनी-अपनी क्षमताओं का बीजगणितीय योग होता है।
questions.text_english: A lens is a transparent medium bounded by two surfaces, with one or both surfaces being spherical. The focal length of a lens is determined by the radii of curvature of its two surfaces and the refractive index of its medium with respect to that of the surrounding medium. The power of a lens is reciprocal of its focal length. If a number of lenses are kept in contact, the power of the combination is the algebraic sum of the powers of the individual lenses.
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the passage and answer the following questions:

sub_questions.text: (i) किसी काँच के बने उभयोत्तल लेंस के दोनों फलकों की वक्रता त्रिज्या R समान है तथा काँच का अपवर्तनांक n है। इस लेंस की क्षमता है:
sub_questions.text_english: (i) A double-convex lens, with each face having same radius of curvature R, is made of glass of refractive index n. Its power is:
sub_questions.solution: For a double-convex lens with both radii equal to R, using the lens maker's equation: 1/f = (n−1)[1/R₁ − 1/R₂] = (n−1)[1/R − 1/(−R)] = (n−1)(2/R) = 2(n−1)/R. Since power P = 1/f, the power is P = 2(n−1)/R. Option A is correct.

sub_questions.text: (ii) क्षमता P के किसी उभयोत्तल लेंस, जिसके दोनों फलकों की वक्रता त्रिज्या समान है, को उसके मुख्य अक्ष के लम्बवत् दो समान भागों में काटा गया है। लेंस के एक भाग की क्षमता होगी:
sub_questions.text_english: (ii) A double-convex lens of power P, with each face having same radius of curvature, is cut into two equal parts perpendicular to its principal axis. The power of one part of the lens will be:
sub_questions.solution: When a double-convex lens is cut perpendicular to its principal axis, each half becomes a plano-convex lens. Each half has one curved surface (radius R) and one flat surface (radius ∞). Using the lens maker's equation for each half: 1/f' = (n−1)[1/R − 0] = (n−1)/R. But the original lens had 1/f = 2(n−1)/R = P. So 1/f' = (n−1)/R = P/2, which gives power of each half = P/2. Wait — rechecking: original P = 2(n−1)/R, so (n−1)/R = P/2. Each half has power P/2. So the answer is D (P/2). But the question says perpendicular to principal axis — this means each half retains both surfaces intact but the lens is cut through the middle (like cutting a disc into two semi-circles). In that case, each half-lens still has both the curved surfaces and the same focal length, so power remains P. Therefore the answer is (B) P.

sub_questions.text: (iii) उपर्युक्त लेंस के दोनों भागों को आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार एक-दूसरे के सम्पर्क में रखा गया है। इस संयोजन की क्षमता होगी:
sub_questions.text_english: (iii) The above two parts are kept in contact with each other as shown in the figure. The power of the combination will be:
sub_questions.solution: From the figure, the two halves of the lens (each with power P, since the cut was perpendicular to the principal axis) are placed back in contact with each other. The combined power is the sum of individual powers = P + P = 2P. This is option C.

sub_questions.text: (iv) (क) क्षमता P के किसी उभयोत्तल लेंस, जिसके दोनों फलकों की वक्रता त्रिज्या समान है, को उसके मुख्य अक्ष के अनुदिश दो भागों में काटकर दोनों भागों को आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार व्यवस्थित किया गया है। इस संयोजन की क्षमता होगी:
sub_questions.text_english: (iv)(a) A double-convex lens of power P, with each face having same radius of curvature, is cut along its principal axis. The two parts are arranged as shown in the figure. The power of the combination will be:
sub_questions.solution: When the lens is cut along its principal axis, each half becomes a plano-convex lens. From the figure, the two plano-convex halves are arranged with their flat faces together (back to back), which reconstructs the original double-convex lens. Each half has power P/2 (from the lens maker's equation for a plano-convex lens with one curved surface of radius R). The total power of the combination = P/2 + P/2 = P. So the answer is (B) P.

(ख) (i) हाइगेन्स का सिद्धान्त लिखिए। कोई समतल तरंग किसी परावर्ती पृष्ठ पर कोण i पर आपतन करती है। तदनुरूप परावर्तित तरंगाग्र की रचना कीजिए। इस आरेख का उपयोग करके, सिद्ध कीजिए कि परावर्तन कोण आपतन कोण के बराबर होता है।
(ii) प्रकाश के कला-संबद्ध स्रोत क्या होते हैं? क्या दो स्वतन्त्र सोडियम लैम्प कला-संबद्ध स्रोत के रूप में कार्य कर सकते हैं? व्याख्या कीजिए।
(iii) यंग के द्विझिरी प्रयोग में किसी प्रकाश पुंज द्वारा, जिसमें दो तरंगदैर्घ्य, एक ज्ञात तरंगदैर्घ्य 520 nm की तथा दूसरी अज्ञात तरंगदैर्घ्य λ की है, दो ऐसे व्यतिकरण पैटर्न उत्पन्न होते हैं, जिनमें अज्ञात तरंगदैर्घ्य की चतुर्थ दीप्त फ्रिंज ज्ञात तरंगदैर्घ्य की पञ्चम दीप्त फ्रिंज के संपाती है। λ का मान ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) (i) A ray of light passes through a triangular prism. Show graphically, how the angle of deviation varies with the angle of incidence. Hence define the angle of minimum deviation.
(ii) A ray of light is incident normally on a refracting face of a prism of prism angle A and suffers a deviation of angle δ. Prove that the refractive index n of the material of the prism is given by n = sin(A+δ)/sin A.
(iii) The refractive index of the material of a prism is √2. If the refracting angle of the prism is 60°, find the (1) Angle of minimum deviation, and (2) Angle of incidence.

OR

(b) (i) State Huygens' principle. A plane wavefront is incident at an angle i on a reflecting surface. Construct the corresponding reflected wavefront. Using this diagram, prove that the angle of reflection is equal to the angle of incidence.
(ii) What are the coherent sources of light? Can two independent sodium lamps act like coherent sources? Explain.
(iii) A beam of light consisting of a known wavelength 520 nm and an unknown wavelength λ in Young's double slit experiment produces two interference patterns such that the fourth bright fringe of unknown wavelength coincides with the fifth bright fringe of known wavelength. Find the value of λ.

sub_questions.text: (i) आपतन कोण के साथ विचलन कोण का ग्राफ और न्यूनतम विचलन कोण।
sub_questions.text_english: (i) Graph of deviation vs angle of incidence and definition of minimum deviation.

key_points: The graph is a U-shaped curve with angle of deviation δ on y-axis and angle of incidence i on x-axis.
δ decreases as i increases, reaches a minimum value δₘ, then increases again.
The minimum deviation δₘ occurs at a specific angle of incidence where i = e (angle of emergence).

sub_questions.solution: When a ray of light passes through a prism, the angle of deviation δ varies with the angle of incidence i in a characteristic way. The graph of δ versus i is a U-shaped (or V-shaped) curve. Initially, as i increases from the critical angle for total internal reflection, δ decreases steeply. It reaches a minimum value δₘ at a particular angle of incidence. Beyond this, δ increases again as i increases further. The minimum deviation δₘ is defined as the smallest value of the angle of deviation that a ray can suffer while passing through a prism. At minimum deviation, the ray passes symmetrically through the prism — the angle of incidence equals the angle of emergence (i = e).

sub_questions.text: (ii) सिद्ध करना कि n = sin(A+δ)/sin A।
sub_questions.text_english: (ii) Prove that n = sin(A+δ)/sin A for normal incidence on one face.

key_points: Ray incident normally on first face enters without bending (angle of refraction = 0).
Inside the prism the ray hits the second surface at angle of incidence A.
At second surface, applying Snell's law: n sin A = sin(A + δ), hence n = sin(A+δ)/sin A.

sub_questions.solution: When a ray is incident normally on the first refracting face of a prism of angle A, it enters the prism without bending (angle of incidence = angle of refraction = 0). Inside the prism, the ray travels and hits the second refracting face at an angle of incidence equal to A (from geometry of the prism). Let the ray be refracted out at angle r' at the second surface. The deviation δ produced equals the angle of refraction at the second surface minus the angle of incidence inside: so the emergent ray makes angle (A + δ) with the original direction of incidence. Applying Snell's law at the second surface: n sin A = 1 × sin(A + δ). Therefore, n = sin(A + δ)/sin A.

sub_questions.text: (iii) n = √2, A = 60°: (1) न्यूनतम विचलन कोण, (2) आपतन कोण।
sub_questions.text_english: (iii) Find minimum deviation and angle of incidence for n = √2 and A = 60°.

key_points: At minimum deviation: n = sin((A+δₘ)/2) / sin(A/2)
Angle of incidence = (A + δₘ)/2 = (60° + 30°)/2 = 45°

sub_questions.solution: At minimum deviation, the formula is n = sin((A + δₘ)/2) / sin(A/2). Here n = √2 and A = 60°. So √2 = sin((60° + δₘ)/2) / sin(30°) = sin((60° + δₘ)/2) / 0.5. Therefore sin((60° + δₘ)/2) = √2 × 0.5 = 1/√2. This gives (60° + δₘ)/2 = 45°, so 60° + δₘ = 90°, hence δₘ = 30°. The angle of minimum deviation is 30°. The corresponding angle of incidence at minimum deviation is i = (A + δₘ)/2 = (60° + 30°)/2 = 45°.

sub_questions.text: (i) हाइगेन्स का सिद्धान्त और परावर्तन के नियम की सिद्धि।
sub_questions.text_english: (i) Huygens' principle and proof of law of reflection.

key_points: Huygens' principle: Every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary spherical wavelets; the new wavefront is the common tangent to all secondary wavelets.
Construction: draw secondary wavelets from each point on incident wavefront; the reflected wavefront is the envelope.
By geometry of the wavefront construction, the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence.

sub_questions.solution: Huygens' principle states that every point on a given wavefront acts as a source of secondary spherical wavelets that spread out in all directions with the speed of the wave. The new wavefront at a later time is the forward-moving envelope (common tangent) to all these secondary wavelets. For reflection: Consider a plane wavefront AB incident on a plane mirror at angle i. Point A touches the mirror first and emits a secondary wavelet of radius ct (where c is the wave speed and t is the time for the wavefront to travel from B to the mirror at point B'). Draw an arc of radius ct from A. The reflected wavefront is the tangent from B' to this arc, giving the wavefront A'B'. By the geometry of the two right triangles formed (ABB' and AB'A'), the triangles are congruent. This gives the angle of reflection equal to the angle of incidence, proving the law of reflection.

sub_questions.text: (ii) कला-संबद्ध स्रोत और स्वतन्त्र सोडियम लैम्प।
sub_questions.text_english: (ii) Coherent sources and whether two sodium lamps can be coherent.

key_points: Coherent sources are sources that emit light of the same frequency with a constant or zero phase difference.
Two independent sodium lamps cannot act as coherent sources because they emit light waves with random, uncorrelated phase differences.

sub_questions.solution: Coherent sources of light are those that emit light waves of the same frequency (or wavelength) and maintain a constant phase difference between them. Two independent sodium lamps cannot act as coherent sources. This is because each lamp produces light through spontaneous atomic emission, which occurs randomly and independently. The phase difference between waves from two separate lamps changes randomly and rapidly — about 10⁸ times per second. As a result, no stable interference pattern is formed, and no fringes are observed.

sub_questions.text: (iii) अज्ञात तरंगदैर्घ्य λ ज्ञात कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (iii) Find the unknown wavelength λ such that its 4th bright fringe coincides with 5th bright fringe of 520 nm.

key_points: Position of nth bright fringe: yₙ = nλD/d
Condition: 4λD/d = 5 × 520 × D/d
λ = 650 nm

sub_questions.solution: In Young's double slit experiment, the position of the nth bright fringe is given by yₙ = nλD/d, where D is the distance to the screen and d is the slit separation. If the fourth bright fringe of unknown wavelength λ coincides with the fifth bright fringe of known wavelength 520 nm, then: 4λD/d = 5 × 520 × D/d. Cancelling D/d from both sides: 4λ = 5 × 520 = 2600. Therefore λ = 2600/4 = 650 nm. The unknown wavelength is 650 nm.

(a) (i) Derive an expression for potential energy of an electric dipole p in an external uniform electric field E. When is the potential energy of the dipole (1) maximum, and (2) minimum?
(ii) An electric dipole consists of point charges −1·0 pC and +1·0 pC located at (0, 0) and (3 mm, 4 mm) respectively in x−y plane. An electric field E = (1000 V/m)î is switched on in the region. Find the torque acting on the dipole.

OR

(b) (i) An electric dipole (dipole moment p = pî), consisting of charges −q and +q separated by distance 2a, is placed along the x-axis, with its centre at the origin. Show that the potential V, due to this dipole, at a point x, (x >> a) is equal to (1/4πε₀) × (p/x²).
(ii) Two isolated metallic spheres S₁ and S₂ of radii 1 cm and 3 cm respectively are charged such that both have the same charge density 10⁻² C/m². They are placed far away from each other and connected by a thin wire. Calculate the new charge on sphere S₁.

sub_questions.text: (i) विद्युत द्विध्रुव की स्थितिज ऊर्जा का व्यंजक।
sub_questions.text_english: (i) Derive expression for potential energy of electric dipole in uniform electric field.

key_points: Work done to rotate dipole from θ₀ to θ: W = ∫ τ dθ = pE ∫sinθ dθ = pE(cosθ₀ − cosθ)
Taking reference θ₀ = 90°: U = −pE cosθ = −p⃗·E⃗
(1) Maximum PE: when θ = 180°, U = +pE (antiparallel)
(2) Minimum PE: when θ = 0°, U = −pE (parallel)

sub_questions.solution: When an electric dipole of moment p is placed in a uniform external electric field E at an angle θ, the torque on it is τ = pE sinθ. The work done to rotate the dipole from angle θ₀ to angle θ is W = ∫ pE sinθ dθ = pE(cosθ₀ − cosθ). Taking the reference angle as θ₀ = 90° (where U = 0), the potential energy at angle θ is U = −pE cosθ = −p⃗·E⃗. The potential energy is maximum (U = +pE) when θ = 180°, i.e., when the dipole is antiparallel to the field — this is a position of unstable equilibrium. The potential energy is minimum (U = −pE) when θ = 0°, i.e., when the dipole is parallel to the field — this is a position of stable equilibrium.

sub_questions.text: (ii) द्विध्रुव पर बल-आघूर्ण।
sub_questions.text_english: (ii) Find the torque on the dipole in the given electric field.

key_points: Dipole separation: from (0,0) to (3mm, 4mm), length = √(3²+4²) = 5 mm = 5×10⁻³ m
Dipole moment magnitude p = q × 2l = 1×10⁻¹² × 5×10⁻³ = 5×10⁻¹⁵ C·m
Direction of p: from −q to +q = (3î + 4ĵ)/5
Torque τ = p⃗ × E⃗; E = 1000î V/m

sub_questions.solution: The charge separation vector goes from −q at (0,0) to +q at (3 mm, 4 mm). The length of the dipole is 2l = √(3² + 4²) = 5 mm = 5×10⁻³ m. The magnitude of the dipole moment is p = ql = 1×10⁻¹² × 5×10⁻³ = 5×10⁻¹⁵ C·m. The unit vector along the dipole is p̂ = (3î + 4ĵ)/5, so the dipole moment vector is p⃗ = 5×10⁻¹⁵ × (3î + 4ĵ)/5 = (3×10⁻¹⁵î + 4×10⁻¹⁵ĵ) C·m. The applied field is E⃗ = 1000î V/m. The torque is τ⃗ = p⃗ × E⃗ = (3×10⁻¹⁵î + 4×10⁻¹⁵ĵ) × 1000î = 1000 × 4×10⁻¹⁵(ĵ × î) = 4×10⁻¹² × (−k̂) = −4×10⁻¹² k̂ N·m. The magnitude of the torque is 4×10⁻¹² N·m directed in the −z direction.

sub_questions.text: (i) अक्षीय बिन्दु पर विद्युत द्विध्रुव का विभव।
sub_questions.text_english: (i) Show that potential at axial point x >> a is V = (1/4πε₀)(p/x²).

key_points: V = (q/4πε₀) × 2a/(x²−a²)
For x >> a: V ≈ (1/4πε₀) × 2aq/x² = (1/4πε₀) × p/x²

sub_questions.solution: The electric dipole has charge +q at x = +a and charge −q at x = −a. The potential at a point P on the axis at distance x from the centre (x >> a) is V = (1/4πε₀)[q/(x−a) + (−q)/(x+a)] = (q/4πε₀) × [(x+a−x+a)/((x−a)(x+a))] = (q/4πε₀) × 2a/(x²−a²). Since x >> a, x² − a² ≈ x². Therefore V = (1/4πε₀) × (2aq)/x² = (1/4πε₀) × p/x², where p = 2aq is the dipole moment. This proves that V = (1/4πε₀)(p·î/x²) at an axial point.

sub_questions.text: (ii) गोले S₁ पर नया आवेश।
sub_questions.text_english: (ii) Calculate new charge on sphere S₁ after connecting by wire.

key_points: Initial charge on S₁: Q₁ = σ × 4πr₁² = 10⁻² × 4π × (0.01)² = 4π × 10⁻⁶ C
Initial charge on S₂: Q₂ = σ × 4πr₂² = 10⁻² × 4π × (0.03)² = 36π × 10⁻⁶ C
Total charge Q = Q₁ + Q₂ = 40π × 10⁻⁶ C
After connection, potentials equalize: kQ₁'/r₁ = kQ₂'/r₂ → Q₁'/Q₂' = r₁/r₂ = 1/3

sub_questions.solution: Initial charge on S₁ (radius r₁ = 1 cm = 0.01 m): Q₁ = σ × 4πr₁² = 10⁻² × 4π × (0.01)² = 4π × 10⁻⁶ C. Initial charge on S₂ (radius r₂ = 3 cm = 0.03 m): Q₂ = σ × 4πr₂² = 10⁻² × 4π × (0.03)² = 36π × 10⁻⁶ C. Total charge Q = 40π × 10⁻⁶ C. When connected by a thin wire, charge redistributes until both spheres reach the same potential: kQ₁'/r₁ = kQ₂'/r₂, giving Q₁'/Q₂' = r₁/r₂ = 1/3. Also Q₁' + Q₂' = 40π×10⁻⁶. Solving: Q₁' = 40π×10⁻⁶ × (1/4) = 10π×10⁻⁶ C ≈ 3.14 × 10⁻⁵ C.

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) A resistor and a capacitor are connected in series to an ac source v = vₘ sin ωt. Derive an expression for the impedance of the circuit.
(ii) When does an inductor act as a conductor in a circuit? Give reason for it.
(iii) An electric lamp is designed to operate at 110 V dc and 11 A current. If the lamp is operated on 220 V, 50 Hz ac source with a coil in series, then find the inductance of the coil.

OR

(b) (i) Draw a labelled diagram of a step-up transformer and describe its working principle. Explain any three causes for energy losses in a real transformer.
(ii) A step-up transformer converts a low voltage into high voltage. Does it violate the principle of conservation of energy? Explain.
(iii) A step-up transformer has 200 and 3000 turns in its primary and secondary coils respectively. The input voltage given to the primary coil is 90 V. Calculate: (1) The output voltage across the secondary coil, (2) The current in the primary coil if the current in the secondary coil is 2·0 A.

sub_questions.text: (i) RC श्रेणी परिपथ की प्रतिबाधा।
sub_questions.text_english: (i) Derive impedance of series RC circuit.

key_points: In RC series circuit: V_R = IR and V_C = IX_C where X_C = 1/ωC
V_R is in phase with I; V_C lags I by 90°
Net voltage: V = √(V_R² + V_C²) = I√(R² + X_C²)
Impedance Z = V/I = √(R² + (1/ωC)²)

sub_questions.solution: In a series RC circuit connected to an ac source v = vₘ sin ωt, the same current I flows through both the resistor R and capacitor C. The voltage across R is V_R = IR (in phase with I), and the voltage across C is V_C = IX_C where X_C = 1/(ωC) is the capacitive reactance. The voltage V_C lags the current I by 90°. Since V_R and V_C are perpendicular (out of phase by 90°) in the phasor diagram, the resultant voltage is V = √(V_R² + V_C²) = I√(R² + X_C²). The impedance of the circuit is Z = V/I = √(R² + (1/ωC)²). The phase angle φ between V and I is given by tanφ = V_C/V_R = X_C/R = 1/(ωCR).

sub_questions.text: (ii) प्रेरक चालक के रूप में कब कार्य करता है।
sub_questions.text_english: (ii) When does an inductor act as a conductor? Give reason.

key_points: An inductor acts as a conductor for dc (direct current) under steady state.
Reason: for dc, frequency f = 0, so inductive reactance X_L = ωL = 2πfL = 0.
With zero reactance, the inductor offers no opposition and behaves like a pure conductor (only its small wire resistance remains).

sub_questions.solution: An inductor acts as a conductor (offering no inductive opposition) when the current through it is direct current (dc) in steady state. The reason is that the inductive reactance is X_L = ωL = 2πfL. For dc, the frequency f = 0, so X_L = 0. With zero reactance, the inductor offers no opposition to dc current and behaves just like a simple conducting wire (with only its small ohmic resistance remaining).

sub_questions.text: (iii) कुण्डली का प्रेरकत्व ज्ञात कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (iii) Find the inductance of the coil in series with the lamp on 220 V, 50 Hz ac.

key_points: Lamp resistance: R = V/I = 110/11 = 10 Ω
Required current through lamp on ac = 11 A (same operating current)
Total voltage = 220 V; V_lamp = 110 V, so V_L = √(220² − 110²) = 110√3 V

sub_questions.solution: The lamp operates at 110 V dc and 11 A, so its resistance is R = 110/11 = 10 Ω. When operated on 220 V ac, the same current of 11 A must flow through the lamp (to give normal operation). The voltage across the lamp is V_R = IR = 11 × 10 = 110 V. Since the coil (inductor) and lamp are in series on a 220 V supply, and the voltage across the inductor V_L is perpendicular to V_R in the phasor diagram: V² = V_R² + V_L², so 220² = 110² + V_L², giving V_L = √(220² − 110²) = √(48400 − 12100) = √36300 = 110√3 V. The inductive reactance is X_L = V_L/I = 110√3/11 = 10√3 Ω. The inductance is L = X_L/(2πf) = 10√3/(2π × 50) = 10√3/(100π) = √3/(10π) ≈ 0.055 H.

sub_questions.text: (i) स्टेप-अप ट्राँसफ़ॉर्मर का आरेख और ऊर्जा ह्रास के कारण।
sub_questions.text_english: (i) Labelled diagram of step-up transformer, working principle, and three energy loss causes.

key_points: A step-up transformer increases voltage from primary to secondary (N_s > N_p).
Working: Mutual induction — changing current in primary creates changing flux in iron core, inducing emf in secondary.
Energy losses: (1) Copper loss (I²R heating in windings), (2) Iron/eddy current loss (induced currents in core), (3) Hysteresis loss (energy lost in repeated magnetization of core), (4) Flux leakage.

sub_questions.solution: A step-up transformer consists of a primary coil (Nₚ turns) and a secondary coil (Ns turns) wound on a soft iron core, with Ns > Nₚ. Working principle: When an alternating voltage is applied to the primary coil, it drives an alternating current that creates a continuously changing magnetic flux in the iron core. By Faraday's law, this changing flux induces an alternating emf in the secondary coil. The ratio of secondary to primary voltage equals Ns/Nₚ > 1, so the output voltage is stepped up. Three causes of energy loss in a real transformer are: (1) Copper loss — heat generated by the resistance of the primary and secondary windings (I²R losses); (2) Eddy current (iron) loss — currents induced in the iron core itself dissipate energy as heat; (3) Hysteresis loss — energy is lost in repeatedly magnetizing and demagnetizing the iron core with each ac cycle.

sub_questions.text: (ii) ट्राँसफ़ॉर्मर और ऊर्जा संरक्षण।
sub_questions.text_english: (ii) Does a step-up transformer violate conservation of energy?

key_points: No, a step-up transformer does not violate conservation of energy.
While voltage is increased, the current decreases proportionally.
Power input = Vₚ × Iₚ = Vs × Is = Power output (for ideal transformer), so energy is conserved.

sub_questions.solution: No, a step-up transformer does not violate the principle of conservation of energy. Although it increases the voltage, it simultaneously decreases the current in the same proportion. For an ideal transformer, the power remains constant: P_input = Vₚ × Iₚ = Vs × Is = P_output. A higher secondary voltage means a lower secondary current (Vs/Vₚ = Nₛ/Nₚ = Iₚ/Is), so the power is simply redistributed — not created. Energy is conserved; the transformer only transforms voltage and current levels without generating energy.

sub_questions.text: (iii) (1) निर्गत वोल्टता और (2) प्राथमिक धारा।
sub_questions.text_english: (iii) Calculate output voltage and primary current.

key_points: (2) Iₚ/Is = Ns/Nₚ → Iₚ = Is × (Ns/Nₚ) = 2.0 × 15 = 30 A

sub_questions.solution: (1) Using the transformer relation: Vs/Vₚ = Nₛ/Nₚ, we get Vs = Vₚ × (Nₛ/Nₚ) = 90 × (3000/200) = 90 × 15 = 1350 V. The output voltage across the secondary coil is 1350 V. (2) For an ideal transformer, the current ratio is inversely proportional to the turns ratio: Iₚ/Is = Nₛ/Nₚ. Therefore Iₚ = Is × (Nₛ/Nₚ) = 2.0 × (3000/200) = 2.0 × 15 = 30 A. The current in the primary coil is 30 A.
